# Critique — Pattern 6 (Reproductive)

The slot allocation across the 255 slots was distributed as follows: Anatomy & Surgical History (~10%), Pregnancy & Cyclic Context (~15%), Menstrual & Hormonal Health (~15%), Fertility & Contraception (~10%), Sexual Health & Preventative Screening (~20%), and self-monitoring/lifecycle fillers (~30%). The question regarding ever having had a pregnancy termination (abortion) came closest to the scope exclusion line, but was kept as a single yes/no historical flag, avoiding all sensitive clinical and jurisdictional details. Inclusive phrasing was handled by referencing anatomical functions neutrally (e.g., "Do you currently experience regular menstrual periods?") rather than assuming gender identity, and framing gender-affirming care simply as neutral medical history (e.g., estrogen or testosterone therapy). Overlaps exist with the Metabolic and Genetics domains (e.g., PCOS diagnosis, BRCA gene status) because endocrine and genetic risk factors are core elements of reproductive medicine. The V-flag was systematically applied to questions representing protective screening compliance (e.g., recent cervical screening, HPV vaccination) or constructive contraception habits to align with the risk-present polarity model. We paraphrased elements of the EPDS and Greene Climacteric Scale to maintain the author's voice without copyright issues. The weakest question is position 253 ("Do you log your reproductive symptoms weekly...") as it carries low clinical utility compared to specific physiological markers.
